section_summary.extract_value: This abstract reports one study of 261 college students (mean age 20.16, 60.9% female) from a non-residential college in the northeastern United States who completed a questionnaire measuring body appreciation, interest in cosmetic enhancements, and need for uniqueness. Findings indicate higher body appreciation and being African American/Black were associated with greater self-attributed need for uniqueness and investment in a distinctive appearance, while body appreciation was not significantly associated with interest in cosmetic enhancements. The section does not label any study as 'Study 1' and describes a single study/sample.

The association between body appreciation and interest in cosmetic enhancements (e.g., hair coloring) was not significant.'
